caCert.title: CA Certificate Setup Required
caCert.intro: To intercept and analyze HTTPS traffic, Kiji Privacy Proxy uses a self-signed Certificate Authority (CA). You must trust this certificate on your system and/or browsers.
caCert.revealDesktopOnly: Reveal in Finder is only available in the desktop app.
caCert.revealFailed: Failed to open the certificate folder.

system.commandHelp: This command requires administrator privileges and will install the certificate system-wide.

steps.s1: Double-click the certificate file: ~/Library/Application Support/Kiji Privacy Proxy/certs/ca.crt
steps.s2: This opens Keychain Access - click Add to install
steps.s3: In Keychain Access, select System keychain in the left sidebar
steps.s4: Search for "Kiji Privacy Proxy CA" and double-click it
steps.s5: Click the ▶ triangle next to "Trust" to expand the section
steps.s6: Set "When using this certificate" to "Always Trust"
steps.s8: Close the window and enter your password when prompted

system.important: Important: You must restart your browser after trusting the certificate. System-wide trust works for Safari and Chrome. Firefox requires separate configuration (see Browser-Specific tab).
system.commonIssue: ⚠️ Common Issue: If the certificate shows "Number of trust settings: 0" in terminal, it means you haven't set it to "Always Trust" in steps 6-7 above. The certificate must be marked as trusted for SSL, not just installed.

browsers.chromeTip: Tip: Chrome on macOS typically uses the system keychain, so system-wide trust (see other tab) should be sufficient.
